HYPOTHESIS (data-grounded, on the recoverable binary structure of the obfuscated Q8 items):

"The two roles with the highest proportion of association with requirements in ML-enabled systems are the **Project Lead** and the **Data Scientist**. Among survey respondents who answered the Q8 page (n=194 valid of 276, after excluding the '-77' no-response code per the approved domain-knowledge rule), 51.03% flagged the Project Lead role as addressing ML-aspect requirements ('quoted', 95% bootstrap CI [43.81%, 58.25%]) and 48.97% flagged the Data Scientist (95% CI [41.75%, 56.19%]). The pair {Project Lead, Data Scientist} constituted the top two roles in 100% of 10,000 bootstrap replicates — every other role is far behind (Business Analyst, the next-closest, at 25.77%) — so the top-two identity is extremely stable. The two leaders are close to each other and their bootstrap CIs overlap (Project Lead edges Data Scientist 68.3% vs 31.7% of top-1 draws but the difference is not statistically significant), so the claim is safely the co-top-two pair rather than a strict ordering. CAVEAT: the Q8 addressing items in the supplied file are obfuscated (each cell is only '-77', 'quoted', or 'not quoted'), so the headline proportions 49.6% and 61.389% cited in the question — and their sub-percentage-point confidence intervals (which would need an effective n≈60,000) — cannot be reproduced from this file, and the exact mapping of 'quoted' to the original Likert-frequency labels is unknown; the result therefore stands on the stable rank ordering recovered from the binary 'quoted' signal, not on the original scale values."

ROBUSTNESS NOTES (reported plainly): the top-two pair survives the 'quoted'+all-276-denominator variant (same pair: 35.87% and 34.42%) and is supported by the monotone cross-tab (respondents most often flag their own role as addressing ML aspects: Data Scientist 74.6%, Solution Architect 75.0%, Project Lead 62.5%, Business Analyst 50.0%, Developer 45.5%). Under the inverted indicator ('not quoted' as association) the ranking reverses to {Tester, Others} — an obviously domain-implausible outcome that supports 'quoted' as the meaning-bearing direction. Because this direction assumption is what drives the ranking, and the original scale is unrecoverable, the top-two claim is conditional on 'quoted' = positively indicated.

payload.workflow: 1) Inspected data/requirements_engineering_for_ML-enabled_systems.csv (276 respondents x 202 cols). 2) Detected obfuscation: the 8 Q8_ML_Addressing_* role items (and 104 other matrices/indicator blocks) contain only the tokens '-77','quoted','not quoted'; verified at raw-byte level; '-77' = no-response (same 82 of 276 respondents on all 8 items), so valid n per role = 194. 3) Primary analysis: per-role proportion of 'quoted' (positively indicated role) among valid respondents (194), for all eight roles. 4) Uncertainty quantification: nonparametric bootstrap at the respondent (row) level, B=10,000, fixed seed 42, percentile 2.5th-97.5th 95% CIs, plus rank-stability (top-1 / top-2 shares and joint top-2 pair frequency across replicates). 5) Sensitivities: (a) 'not quoted' as the association indicator (reversed ranking, domain-implausible); (b) 'quoted' with all-276 denominator (same top-2 pair); (c) 'quoted' x respondent D4_Role cross-tab showing monotone own-role endorsement that supports 'quoted' as meaning-bearing. 6) Deliverable: natural-language hypothesis naming Project Lead and Data Scientist as the two roles with the highest proportion of association with requirements, with explicit caveat that the 49.6%/61.389% headline values and sub-percentage-point CIs are not reproducible from the obfuscated file. Executed artifact: analysis.py.
payload.hypothesis: The two roles with the highest proportion of association with requirements in ML-enabled systems are the Project Lead (51.0% of valid respondents, bootstrap 95% CI [43.8%, 58.2%]) and the Data Scientist (49.0%, CI [41.8%, 56.2%]); they were the top-two pair in 100% of 10,000 bootstrap replicates, far ahead of all other roles (Business Analyst third at 25.8%). Caveat: the Q8 addressing items are obfuscated in the supplied file, so the exact 49.6% and 61.389% headline proportions and their narrow CIs cannot be reproduced here; the claim rests on the recovered binary 'quoted' (positively indicated) signal and the stable top-two rank ordering.
